data.title: ASEAN+3 agrees on initiative to explore crypto payments cooperation
data.description:
China, Japan, South Korea and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) will establish a working group aimed at enhancing connectivity between domestic digital payment networks and bringing their regulatory approaches into more alignment.

The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) will oversee the program, according to a statement issued by Japan’s Ministry of Finance.

The agreement was reached at the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies’ Meeting in Kyoto that concluded on Thursday.

Cointelegraph, meanwhile, reported on Friday that Binance co-founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao favors crypto license passporting across ASEAN, arguing that firms regulated in one market should be able to enter others through a simplified approval process rather than applying from scratch.

While moving toward greater cooperation, member states still regulate digital assets separately, creating multiple approval processes for companies seeking a regional presence.

Speaking at a fireside chat at the ASEAN Tech Summit Manila 2026, Zhao backed an idea raised by FinTech Alliance PH founding chair Lito Villanueva for regulatory passporting or license portability.

A regional licensing framework could reduce compliance costs, encourage competition and make it easier for crypto and stablecoin services to operate across ASEAN’s fragmented regulatory markets.

Magazine: AI agents are using credit cards. Where does that leave crypto?

data.title: Conservatives set to win government in Australia's second-most populous state
data.description:
Conservatives were on track to win an election in the Australian state of Victoria on Saturday, throwing out a deeply unpopular Labor government after more than a decade while denying anti-immigration populist party One Nation the breakthrough many supporters had hoped for.

The centre-right Liberal-National coalition was set to win a majority of the state's 88 lower house seats based on early vote counting, according to projections by the Australian Broadcasting Corp, ending 12 years of Labor rule in a state long regarded as one of the centre-left party's strongest bastions.

data.title: Chainlink Reserve Nears 7 Million LINK as Treasury Adds 122K Tokens: Can LINK Price Reclaim $10?
data.description:
Chainlink’s growing strategic reserve is drawing fresh attention as its holdings approach 7 million LINK, highlighting the network’s expanding revenue-linked token accumulation mechanism. The latest deposit of 122,450 tokens brings the reserve closer to another milestone, even as LINK struggles to recover from its October peak. While continued accumulation strengthens the network’s long-term economic narrative, the token’s price structure remains under pressure.

Investors are now watching whether reserve growth, institutional adoption and broader market demand can help LINK price reclaim the $10 level.

Chainlink Reserve Adds 122K LINK as Holdings Approach 7 Million

Chainlink’s strategic reserve received another 122,450 LINK on November 26, bringing its total holdings to approximately 6.93 million tokens. The latest addition was worth around $1.1 million at the time of the transaction, according to the reserve’s on-chain activity. Its total value stood near $64.9 million at a LINK price of $9.37 in the latest reserve dashboard data.

BSCN
@BSCNews

Chainlink's official reserve approaches 7M COINBASE:LINKUSD.@Chainlink's latest reserve purchase arrived yesterday, when it added some 122,450 COINBASE:LINKUSD to the treasury.

The Reserve now holds some 6.93M COINBASE:LINKUSD tokens valued at around $66.2M.

The company is yet to spend or sell a single token… pic.twitter.com/3CsyIr2ob2

Nov 27, 2026

The reserve is funded through Chainlink’s revenue from enterprise integrations and on-chain services. Its Payment Abstraction mechanism converts eligible payments into LINK before transferring the tokens into the strategic reserve. This creates a direct connection between demand for Chainlink services and the reserve’s accumulation process.

The reserve has maintained a weekly deposit streak since August 2025. Importantly, Chainlink has stated that it does not expect withdrawals from the reserve for multiple years. This makes the mechanism a longer-term accumulation initiative rather than a short-term trading wallet.

Chainlink Adoption and Institutional Expansion Strengthen the Long-Term Narrative

Chainlink’s reserve growth comes as the network expands its role in institutional blockchain infrastructure. Its services cover price feeds, cross-chain interoperability, data services and infrastructure for tokenized assets.

The company’s Q3 2026 review highlighted several developments, including the launch of CCIP 2.0, institutional financing infrastructure through Fulcrum and integrations involving banks and capital-market participants. Chainlink also reported that its reserve surpassed 6 million LINK during the quarter, following the accumulation of more than 1.54 million tokens in Q3.

These developments are important because long-term demand for LINK depends on the actual use of Chainlink services across decentralized finance and traditional financial infrastructure. The strategic reserve provides one mechanism through which network revenue can translate into LINK accumulation.

However, adoption announcements alone do not guarantee token-price appreciation. Investors will need to monitor whether institutional integrations generate recurring service revenue and whether that revenue produces sustained reserve growth.

Chainlink Price Analysis: Can LINK Break Above $10.70?

Chainlink’s daily chart shows LINK trading near $9.15 after a prolonged decline from its October peak around $15–$16. The token has formed a series of lower highs and lower lows, while its moving averages continue to slope downward. This indicates that sellers still control the broader technical structure.

The immediate recovery challenge is the $10.00–$10.80 region. The $10.70–$10.80 as a major supply zone, where previous buying attempts encountered selling pressure. A sustained daily close above this area could improve momentum and open the way towards $12.

On the downside, LINK needs to defend the recent $9 region to maintain its short-term recovery attempt. The broader demand zone sits around $7–$8, making it an important support area if selling pressure returns.

The next directional move will depend on whether buyers can push LINK above $10 and challenge the stronger supply zone. Continued reserve accumulation and institutional adoption offer a constructive long-term narrative, but the trend remains weak until the token reclaims major resistance.

data.title: XRP Ledger Hits 80% Lending Threshold as Deaton Says XRP Has More to Unlock
data.description:
XRP Ledger has cleared a key hurdle for its biggest DeFi expansion that has lacked for years. 80% of Validators now need to show their support for the next 14 days, which could bring native lending to XRPL

Responding to the milestone, CryptoLaw founder John Deaton said XRPL has long offered more than just payments, but the market has yet to fully recognize its wider capabilities.

Lending Vote Moves Into Its Two-Week Countdown

The LendingProtocol amendment has received enough validator support to begin its 14-day activation period on the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

The latest vote shows 30 validators in support, meeting the required 29 votes out of 35 trusted validators. The related upgrades, LendingProtocolV1_1 and SingleAssetVault, also received 30 votes.

However, the upgrade is not live yet.

It needs more than 80% support for 14 straight days. If support falls to 80% or below, the countdown resets. If support holds, LendingProtocol could go live on December 11.

XRPL validator Vet highlighted what the upgrade could unlock, he said,

“Lending and borrowing unlock capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger, provide yield and make XRP and XRPL assets usable as collateral.”

That expands XRPL beyond its long-standing payments and asset-transfer role and gives developers a native foundation for credit markets.

Deaton Sees Lending as the Missing Piece

John Deaton welcomed the lending upgrade, saying he knew very little about XRP or Ripple when he first joined the SEC case. At the time, he owned more Bitcoin and Ethereum. However, the case pushed him to learn more about the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

John E Deaton
@JohnEDeaton1

When I intervened in the @SECGov 🆚 @Ripple case, tbh, I didn’t know very much about #XRP or Ripple. In fact, owned a lot more of #BTC & #ETH than #XRP. For me, the case was more about government overreach and regulatory capture than a specific token. I was right.

During the… https://t.co/2hQ58i5OdF

Nov 27, 2026

He pointed out that XRPL already had a built-in DEX and supported the creation of tokens, making it useful for real-world assets (RWAs). However, it lacked one important feature, lending.

“In short, in 2012, the XRPL was revolutionary. But its DeFi stack was missing one piece: lending. Not anymore.”

If activated, XLS-66 would add lending to XRPL’s existing payment and asset transfer features.

It could also create new uses for the network’s roughly $837 million stablecoin market, with RLUSD making up about 89% of the total supply.

XRP Now Faces the Market’s Biggest Test

The lending upgrade does not guarantee higher XRP demand or a price rise. Its real impact will depend on how many users deposit funds, take loans, and use the new system.

If validator support stays above 80% for the next two weeks, XRPL could activate lending around December 11.

As of now, XRP is trading around $0.942, reflecting a 1.5% drop seen in the last 24 hours.

Delhi High Court sets aside stay on NHAI's 3-year debarment of PNC Infratech
data.description:
Infrastructure company PNC Infratech Ltd on Saturday (November 28) said the Delhi High Court's division bench on Thursday (November 26) set aside, by consent of the parties, an earlier order staying the National Highways Authority of India's (NHAI) three-year debarment of the company and Awadh Expressway Private Ltd.

The court has directed the parties to argue the matter afresh before the single judge, including on the question of interim relief.

A bench comprising Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma passed the order while hearing two appeals filed by NHAI against the October 12, 2026, interim order that had granted relief to PNC Infratech and Awadh Expressway.

The division bench clarified that the matter would be reconsidered without being influenced by its decision to set aside the earlier stay order by consent. This means there is no final adjudication on the merits of NHAI's debarment orders, and the question of interim protection remains open before the single judge.

Court cautions NHAI over conduct of officers

Separately, the division bench expressed concern over the manner in which the proceedings leading to the October 12 order were conducted.

"Having perused the relevant record maintained by the office of the appellant, we have reason to believe that the proceedings which led to the passing of the impugned order were not conducted in a careful and diligent manner," the court said.

The bench also issued a caution to NHAI's highest officer, directing the official to immediately look into the conduct of the officers concerned. All pending applications in the two appeals were also disposed of.

Shares of PNC Infratech Ltd ended at ₹124.30, up by ₹0.15, or 0.12%, on the BSE.

data.title: Long-Term-Care Insurance Promised Them Peace of Mind. It Became a Nightmare. — WSJ
data.description:
By Jean Eaglesham | Photography by Ali Lapetina for WSJ | Design by Annie Ng

The Economics of Growing Old

This story is part of a WSJ series on aging. A new piece will publish each day through Dec. 1.

Lon and Mary Jo Cooke bought insurance 27 years ago to pay the bills if they ever need long-term care. The couple, now in their 80s, wanted their retirement to be worry free.

But their insurance has itself become a financial headache.

This year, the Cookes' insurer, Brighthouse Life Insurance, said it was hiking their premiums 92%, to almost $11,000 a year — unless they agreed to sharp cuts in their long-promised benefits. The Ann Arbor, Mich.-based couple feel trapped.

"The probability of one of us needing care over the next several years is too high to let our policies lapse," Lon Cooke, an 87-year-old Vietnam veteran, said.

Long-term-care insurance is pitched as offering peace of mind. The policies are designed to cover the eye-watering costs of personal care, should you need this — as 60% of women and 53% of men likely will, according to consulting firm Milliman.

The market for this insurance, however, is plagued with poor affordability, lack of accessibility, and fraught claims-handling, a consumer panel of the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, a regulatory body, found in a report this year.

The report's conclusions were blunt: "long-term-care insurance is failing many consumers."

Math problems

Among those failed by the insurers: a generation of Americans, now paying a steep price for an industry error.

Long-term care was the hot new product for insurers in the 1990s. Baby boomers were preparing for retirement, and many saw their own parents' nest eggs depleted by the exorbitant cost of getting old.

Long-term-care policies were a gift to their children, a way to say, don't worry about us.

Except many insurers got the math on the new policies wrong.

"Some insurers started selling these policies just to make sure they didn't miss out on a hot market," said Bonnie Burns, a consultant at California Health Advocates. "I kept saying at the time, 'You can't provide cheap coverage for something that costs this much money.'"

Insurers underestimated how long people would live and how fast healthcare costs would rise. And fewer customers canceled policies than expected.

Many of the original insurers got out of the business and offloaded the policies at a loss, leaving it to a fresh set of investors to manage as customers aged.

Bait and switch

The Cookes bought their policies in 1999 from a unit of Travelers that was sold in 2005 to MetLife. The policies moved again in 2017 to MetLife-spinoff Brighthouse. That insurer in turn is being sold to private-equity firm Aquarian Capital, subject to a signoff by regulators.

Rather than risk high losses pushing companies into insolvency, regulators have allowed insurers to confront policyholders with a stark choice: vertiginous price rises or sweeping cuts to benefits.

"This can create a perceived 'bait and switch' scenario," Amy Killelea, assistant research professor at Georgetown University's McCourt School of Public Policy, said. "Consumers find the benefits they are able to afford are much slimmer than those they were promised."

Lon Cooke this year asked the Virginia Bureau of Insurance to veto Brighthouse's planned near-doubling of premiums, only to be rebuffed. The rise was "justified to ensure the company's ability to pay future claims," the regulator wrote to him.

The Cookes are hanging on to their policies to avoid the problems their own mothers faced when they needed nursing-home care in North Dakota.

Neither of their mothers had insurance: "They were born during the Depression — this wasn't something then," Lon Cooke said.

The bill for the mothers' care — around $500,000 — had to be paid by selling their homes and drawing down their bank accounts, he added. Each left only around $20,000 in her estate.

The Cookes have already paid more than $63,000 on their policies. The 92% hike will take their combined annual premium to $10,826 in 2029: seven times the $1,530 total annual cost when they bought the policies in 1999. That is a far sharper increase than the approximate doubling of consumer prices since that time.

"A lot of older policyholders, like my wife and I, may no longer be able to afford these policies at a time when coverage may be most needed," Lon Cooke said.

Brighthouse offered the Cookes the chance to cut their premiums — if they agreed to forfeit the inflation-proofing of their benefits, capping the daily amount payable at $300, less than the typical $450 cost for a private nursing-home room in their city, according to the American Council on Aging.

The maximum time benefits will be paid would drop from three to two years, while increasing the so-called elimination period before the insurance kicks in from 20 to 100 days.

Another option: pay no more premiums, and cap their total benefit at twice what they have already paid in.

A spokeswoman for Brighthouse Financial, which owns Brighthouse Life Insurance, said it "understands that rate increases may be a challenge for some policyholders, and to provide flexibility, we offer impacted policyholders options to adjust their coverage to meet their needs."

A spokeswoman for the Virginia regulator said it balances consumer protection with ensuring that companies remain solvent. It doesn't have the legal authority to veto a requested rate increase that is actuarially justified, she added.

Dangling incentives for a loss of benefits is a widespread industry practice for older policies.

Genworth Financial, the biggest long-term-care insurer, has what it calls a multiyear "action plan" to mitigate the costs of its older policies. It rewards executives for hitting targets on rate increases and benefit cuts, according to its securities filings.

The plan appears to be working for the company. Genworth said it has achieved $35 billion of benefit reductions and premium increases from 2012 through September, measured in today's money. Almost two-thirds, or 62%, of customers who were offered a cut in benefits agreed to take one, it added.

One of its customers, Annette Schmuecker of Bethel, Conn., was offered a cash payment of up to $1,200, in addition to a cut in premiums, for adjusting her policy's coverage. The alternative: a 122% rate increase, should regulators allow that, Genworth said in a 2023 letter.

Schmuecker bought her policy in 2009 through AARP, believing it would offer the best deal for seniors. The organization, which advocates for retirees, was acting as a conduit for Genworth, in return for undisclosed referral fees.

Schmuecker said the Genworth adviser who sold her the "AARP long-term-care solution" gave the impression any rate increases would be minimal.

She and her husband John, who has a separate long-term-care policy from Transamerica, now pay $20,632 a year for their policies. The couple, retirees in their 70s, are reluctant to give up their "catastrophically expensive" policies, he said.

They have seen the impact on friends who don't have insurance to help care for a spouse who needs care.

"It's a terrible burden," John Schmuecker said. "We've seen families bankrupt."

Genworth in a statement said it understood "how difficult premium increases can be for policyholders, especially later in life." The actions the company has taken on its older long-term-care policies are intended to ensure that it "can continue paying meaningful benefits to policyholders for decades to come," it added.

A spokeswoman for AARP said Genworth stopped sales of AARP-branded plans in 2013. "Particularly in the insurance space, AARP makes clear that individuals need to evaluate carefully the features of any plan," she added.

Claims can be an uphill battle

Making a successful claim is often an uphill battle, consumer advocates say. Many policies offer so-called reimbursement coverage, meaning you have to pay upfront and then claim for each item.

"If you don't do it correctly — file the right paperwork or have mom cared for by the right people — then the contract language could result in a claim denial," said Jesse Slome, director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance, an industry-funded organization that promotes planning for long-term-care needs.

Denials and delays are commonplace, industry filings show.

More than one in 10 initial claims on stand-alone long-term-care policies were denied last year, according to NAIC data. But certain states saw much higher denial rates.

Claimants in Vermont and Michigan faced a one in four chance of their initial claim being denied. Denial rates in another 31 states were 20% or higher, the data show.

Customers can wait months for a check. For stand-alone long-term-care policies, around one in five people last year had to wait more than 60 days for a decision on their claim, the data show.

Alvin Jacobsen of Seattle, a retired executive known as Jake, needed round-the-clock care after developing Alzheimer's disease in his 80s. His long-term-care insurance policy appeared to cover his monthly nursing home fees of over $9,000. But his insurer, John Hancock, took months to issue any payment.

"It felt like they were stalling us," said Meg Jacobsen, his 80-year-old widow.

The insurer demanded reams of invoices, proof of nursing visits and other paperwork, some of which had already been supplied to it several times over, his son Christian Jacobsen said. "There is always another piece of paper needed," he said. "And you never get to talk to the same person twice."

As the claim dragged on, Christian Jacobsen and his wife took out a loan on their home to help pay the spiraling care costs. "We were throwing money down a hole and hoping the hole would fill up at some time," he said.

data.title: Zimbabwe central bank cuts policy rate to 25% in latest easing
data.description:
Zimbabwe's central bank said it had lowered its policy rate from 27.5% to 25% given current and projected low inflation and the need to support economic activity.

  • The rate cut brings the cumulative reduction in the policy rate to 10 percentage points since June 2026, the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe said in the statement dated November 27

  • Inflation is expected to average 4.0% in 2026 and about 5% in 2027, according to the bank's latest projections

  • Annual inflation was 4.3% in November in local currency terms

  • The central bank said its Monetary Policy Committee would remain vigilant to global risks and the effects of the El Nino weather pattern

  • The Southern African country's budget for next year forecasts weaker economic growth because of El Nino, which is expected to cause lower rainfall, affecting agricultural output

data.title: Nykaa partners with Dutch beauty brand Gisou; Here's what's in store
data.description:
A honey-infused hair oil rooted in six generations of beekeeping is now entering India's beauty market. Gisou, the Dutch beauty brand founded by Negin Mirsalehi, has launched in India through an exclusive partnership with Nykaa, bringing its honey-powered haircare and beauty products to Indian consumers.

BEE KEEPING HERITAGE IN INDIA 

Founded in 2015, Gisou draws on Mirsalehi's family beekeeping heritage in the Netherlands, with honey from the family's Bee Garden at the centre of its formulations. The brand's journey began with a homemade honey-infused hair oil and has since expanded into a global beauty business spanning haircare, skincare-inspired beauty and fragrance.

Gisou's founder, Negin Mirsalehi, has positioned the brand around her family's beekeeping legacy, with the business evolving from a personal beauty ritual into an internationally recognised label. The founder-led narrative has also played a role in the brand's identity, combining beauty formulations with storytelling around heritage, craftsmanship and the bee ecosystem.

Speaking about the India launch, Mirsalehi said, “We’re so excited to bring Gisou to India with Nykaa. What began in my family’s Bee Garden with a homemade honey-infused hair oil has grown into a global beauty brand, and bringing that story to India is a very special moment for me.”

She added that the partnership would allow the brand to share its beekeeping heritage and honey-powered beauty rituals with a new consumer community.

NYKAA's GROWING PORTFOLIO

For Nykaa, Gisou adds to its growing portfolio of international premium beauty brands as it continues to use its online platform, physical stores and import-distribution network to bring global labels to India.

Anchit Nayar, Executive Director and CEO of Nykaa Beauty, said, “Gisou is one of the most distinctive and innovative brands in haircare and in beauty today, bringing together a unique heritage and a modern approach to beauty that resonates with consumers around the world.”

Nykaa has increasingly positioned itself as a launch platform for international beauty brands looking to enter India, leveraging its customer base, omnichannel distribution and beauty-focused retail ecosystem. The company reported more than 65 million customers and 338 offline beauty destinations as of September 30, 2026.

The bigger question for consumers who have previously purchased Gisou overseas is whether buying the brand in India comes at a premium.

Some of its best-known products are now listed on Nykaa, with the Honey Infused Hair Oil priced at ₹2,600, the Honey Infused Lip Oil at ₹2,900 and the

Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Hair Mask at ₹4,700.

A comparison with Gisou's European website prices suggests that the Indian pricing is relatively close to international retail pricing.

Gisou will be available exclusively on Nykaa.com and across select Nykaa stores in India. Its arrival adds another premium international label to a market where consumer interest in specialised haircare, global beauty trends and ingredient-led formulations continues to shape brand expansion.

data.title: BPCL approves ₹1.27 lakh crore Andhra Refinery, targets July 2032 for commercial operations
data.description:
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) approved a capital expenditure of ₹1,26,656 crore to establish a greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh. The board cleared this proposal during its meeting held on Saturday, November 28, 2026, according to a BPCL exchange filing.

"In terms of Regulation 30 of SEBI (Listing Obligations & Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and further to the earlier intimation dated 24th December 2024 and 28th October 2025, we wish to inform that the Board at its meeting held on Saturday, 28th November 2026, has accorded its approval for setting up of Greenfield Refinery & Petrochemical Complex and Associated Facilities at Ramayapatnam, Andhra Pradesh through a Wholly Owned Subsidiary (WOS) of the Company, at an estimated gross capital expenditure of ₹1,26,656 crore (+/- 20 per cent estimate), subject to receipt of the applicable Government, Statutory and Regulatory approvals," the filing stated.

The company scheduled the estimated commercial operation of the complex for July 2032. BPCL currently operates an existing capacity of 35.3 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA). Based on the financial year 2025-26, its existing capacity utilisation stood at 116.6 per cent.

The new project adds 9 MMTPA of crude capacity alongside a 1.5 MMTPA mixed-feed ethylene cracker and downstream petrochemical units. This brings the combined throughput to the Ramayapatnam complex to 10.5 MMTPA.

"The integrated configuration comprises a 9 MMTPA refinery, a 1.5 MMTPA mixed-feed ethylene cracker with petrochemical intensity of about 34 per cent," the filing read.

To fund the ₹1,26,656 crore investment, which carries a (+/-) 20 per cent estimate, the company selected a combination of equity and debt through its wholly owned subsidiary. Officials currently finalise these financing arrangements with lenders.

"The Project is intended to address BPCL's widening deficit in key transportation fuels and India's growing petrochemical supply gap," the exchange filing noted.

The company designed the facility to strengthen domestic product availability and curb reliance on overseas markets.

"It is expected to strengthen product availability, reduce import dependence in key polymers, improve value realisation through refinery-petrochemical integration, diversify earnings and support downstream chemical and polymer industries," the filing added.

The project awaits necessary government, statutory, and regulatory clearances before execution proceeds. Through this expansion in Ramayapatnam, BPCL aligned its long-term production capabilities with fuel and polymer demand requirements across the country.

data.title: Groww bets on AI to build 'simple and powerful' investing
data.description:
Groww, one of the key players in the Indian investment horizon today, introduced a new generation of AI-powered products at Groww Next 2026, its flagship technology event.

The company underscored the rising dominance and centrality of artificial intelligence and said that AI is now an integral part of every step in the Groww investing journey, helping customers interpret information, identify what matters, and act at the right time, while leaving the final decision in the investor’s hands.

To sustain the growth of financialisation in India, this shortfall cannot be addressed simply by adding more people. Groww is embedding research-backed intelligence in GR-1 and MF Prime to make expert-level guidance more accessible.

WHAT ARE GR-1 AND MF PRIME?

GR-1 is Groww’s integrated AI investing assistant, launched in October 2026. It helps users research stocks and mutual funds, assess portfolios, and complete supported tasks within the Groww app.

MF Prime is an optional mutual fund advisory feature on Groww, supported by research and AI. It provides personalised fund recommendations and portfolio guidance tailored to users’ risk profiles, investment horizons, and goals.

GR-1, Groww’s in-house AI assistant, now researches, explains and takes action—with user consent—in more than 20 Indian languages. Regional languages account for 15% of daily queries, while voice contributes nearly 20%.

MF Prime offers every investor research-backed mutual fund guidance, combining AI with insights from Groww’s in-house research team.

New products address a range of needs: minor accounts, digital HUF accounts, SIFs, daily and weekly SIPs, a Sell ANY TIME option for bonds, global investing and AI-powered tools for traders.

Groww customers received nearly 30% of India’s IPO allocations this year. More than 2.5 lakh Jio IPO applicants on Groww were making their first-ever market investment.

COMBINING AI AND HUMAN EXPERTISE 

According to Groww, India’s investor population is expanding much faster than the support available to it. An AMFI-Crisil study estimates that India has about one mutual fund distributor for every 4,000 people. The SEBI chairman has said there are approximately 1,000 SEBI-registered investment advisers in the country. As a result, research-based guidance remains out of reach for most investors.

Groww combines artificial intelligence with human expertise. AI provides speed and scale, while the company’s in-house research and product teams provide oversight to help ensure that information delivered to investors is accurate, relevant and responsible.

As Groww noted on stage, more information does not necessarily lead to better decisions. AI should help investors interpret information rather than overwhelm them, while the final decision remains theirs.

FROM D-STREET TO WALL STREET 

With US stocks now available on Groww, customers can invest in more than 10,000 US-listed stocks and ETFs, gaining exposure to over 50 countries using the KYC they have already completed. They are embracing this access with conviction.

When Brazil’s ETFs dropped by as much as 26% in a single day following the country’s election results in October, the MSCI Brazil ETF became the most-traded US stock ETF on Groww. During NVIDIA’s November correction, orders for the stock on Groww rose more than 15-fold from the beginning of the month.

Before Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut on 19 November, Groww opened pre-orders, and more than a lakh users expressed interest on the product page within hours. Encouraged by this response, Groww plans to offer pre-orders for other high-demand global listings as they come to market.

BONDS ON BONDS

Bonds are increasingly becoming a core component of Groww users’ portfolios. A typical Groww bond investor is aged 25 to 35, has been investing for around three years, and holds bonds worth ₹1 lakh or more. To help safeguard investors’ capital, Groww offers only bonds rated BBB+ or higher.

The main concern about bonds has been that funds are locked in. In the past, investors generally had to hold bonds until maturity unless they found a buyer on the exchange. Groww is now rolling out a Sell option that allows customers to exit their bond holdings before maturity at the prevailing market price—whether they need funds or want to pursue another opportunity.

Lalit Keshre, Co-founder and CEO, Groww: “Our customers have grown up with us. The young professional who started a SIP with us years ago is now investing for a child, a family and the future. More information doesn’t always mean better decisions, so we’re using AI to help investors make sense of what matters, while the final call always stays with them. Honestly, we feel we haven’t covered even 1% of our journey.”

Groww customers received nearly 30% of India’s IPO allocations this year. More than 2.5 lakh Jio IPO applicants on Groww were making their first-ever market investment.

COMBINING AI AND HUMAN EXPERTISE 

According to Groww, India’s investor population is expanding much faster than the support available to it. An AMFI-Crisil study estimates that India has about one mutual fund distributor for every 4,000 people. The SEBI chairman has said there are approximately 1,000 SEBI-registered investment advisers in the country. As a result, research-based guidance remains out of reach for most investors.

Groww combines artificial intelligence with human expertise. AI provides speed and scale, while the company’s in-house research and product teams provide oversight to help ensure that information delivered to investors is accurate, relevant and responsible.

As Groww noted on stage, more information does not necessarily lead to better decisions. AI should help investors interpret information rather than overwhelm them, while the final decision remains theirs.

FROM D-STREET TO WALL STREET 

With US stocks now available on Groww, customers can invest in more than 10,000 US-listed stocks and ETFs, gaining exposure to over 50 countries using the KYC they have already completed. They are embracing this access with conviction.

When Brazil’s ETFs dropped by as much as 26% in a single day following the country’s election results in October, the MSCI Brazil ETF became the most-traded US stock ETF on Groww. During NVIDIA’s November correction, orders for the stock on Groww rose more than 15-fold from the beginning of the month.

Before Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut on 19 November, Groww opened pre-orders, and more than a lakh users expressed interest on the product page within hours. Encouraged by this response, Groww plans to offer pre-orders for other high-demand global listings as they come to market.

BONDS ON BONDS

Bonds are increasingly becoming a core component of Groww users’ portfolios. A typical Groww bond investor is aged 25 to 35, has been investing for around three years, and holds bonds worth ₹1 lakh or more. To help safeguard investors’ capital, Groww offers only bonds rated BBB+ or higher.

The main concern about bonds has been that funds are locked in. In the past, investors generally had to hold bonds until maturity unless they found a buyer on the exchange. Groww is now rolling out a Sell option that allows customers to exit their bond holdings before maturity at the prevailing market price—whether they need funds or want to pursue another opportunity.

Lalit Keshre, Co-founder and CEO, Groww: “Our customers have grown up with us. The young professional who started a SIP with us years ago is now investing for a child, a family and the future. More information doesn’t always mean better decisions, so we’re using AI to help investors make sense of what matters, while the final call always stays with them. Honestly, we feel we haven’t covered even 1% of our journey.”

data.title: Monthly Economic Review: Consumption & demand resilient, private investment broadening gradually
data.description:
India’s economic activity maintained broad-based momentum as the economy entered Q3 FY27, supported by domestic demand and industrial activity.

In India's Monthly Economic Review - November for the month of October, released on November 28, the Department of Economic Affairs' report highlighted that high-frequency indicators showed continued strength in October, with robust growth in e-way bill generation, GST collections, electricity consumption and freight movement.

According to the report, consumption also remained supportive: rural spending continued to hold up, while sequential vehicle sales and other indicators signalled sustained underlying demand.

As per the report, the economy entered Q3 FY27 with broad-based momentum - domestic demand + industry supporting growth, despite global uncertainty.

Growth In Industry

The IIP, or Index of Industrial Production, grew 6.7% YoY in September, led by manufacturing. Core Industries (ICI) grew 10.9% YoY in October (up from 8.2% in September). April-October cumulative growth stood at 6.0% vs 2.3% last year.

The growth was led by iron ore (26.4%), coal (23.1%), electricity (21.6%), cement (15.4%), and steel (7.3%). Furthermore, the Manufacturing PMI stayed in expansion in Oct but eased a bit.

CPI (Retail) rose to 6.09% in October, an increase of 55 basis points, driven by food inflation of approximately 9%, an unfavourable base effect, and festive-season demand. WPI surged; fuel and power inflation climbed to 32.8% from 25.8% in September, while crude petroleum and natural gas inflation reached 71%. Meanwhile, 52% of the CPI basket remains below the 4% target.

However, risks persist as a strong El Niño is expected to peak toward the end of 2026, alongside demand from the wedding season. The IOD, in positive territory at 0.8°C, may partly offset these pressures.

MERCHANDISE EXPORTS 

Term Upside Pressures From Base Effects And A Potentially Strong #ElNiño — CNBC-TV18
@CNBCTV18Live

#FinMin On #Economy | Monthly Economic Review

Nov 28, 2026

India's merchandise exports came in at $49.5 billion in October, marking a 45% rise. YoY, the highest-ever monthly value, and the strongest growth in 5 years

This was led by petroleum products rising 140.2%, electronics up 62.7% to $6.6 billion, engineering up 36% to $12.7 billion, and gems & jewellery up 40.1%. Furthermore, services exports came in at $40.5 billion, up 15.2%, with a surplus of $19.8 billion – offsetting 49.6% of the merchandise deficit. The total trade deficit narrowed to $20.1 billion (from $25.2 billion last year).

In addition to that, forex reserves stood at $705.3 billion as of 13 November – 10 months' import cover, 90.6% of external debt. The rupee appreciated 2% in FY27 till 23 Nov, rising 1.7% in November alone.

When we look at the fiscal deficit, the April–September gross tax revenue reached ₹19.8 lakh crore (+6.1%), capital expenditure stood at ₹6.5 lakh crore (+12.7%), and the fiscal deficit was ₹7.1 lakh crore (+24.7%).

CHALLENGES AHEAD 

As for jobs, the unemployment rate was 4.9% in October, down from 5.2% a year earlier. Here, white-collar hiring, as measured by the Naukri Index, rose 14% year over year in October to 2,836. And MGNREGA demand increased 82.3% year over year, suggesting rural stress and greater demand for work.

As per the report, the Q3 momentum is expected to persist, supported by consumption, new orders, and rural demand. Key risks include the Middle East conflict, shipping risks in the Strait of Hormuz, uncertainty around global trade policy, and oil-price volatility. The Indian crude basket averaged $119.9 per barrel in October, compared with $65.1 a year earlier, although it had fallen below $100 by early November.

Economic buffers remain strong, including high foreign-exchange reserves, resilient exports, and policy support for manufacturing in critical minerals, electronics, energy storage, and containers.

FINANCE MINISTRY SAYS INDIA CAN NAVIGATE CHALLENGES 

According to the Finance Ministry, it sees upside risks to inflation in the coming months but hopes that crude oil below $100 and recent rupee strength will help ward off pressures. Inflation may face near-term upside pressures like the base effect, possibly a strong El Niño.

The continued conflict in West Asia & risks to the Strait of Hormuz may keep oil bills and freight rates volatile. Furthermore, the supply-side shocks threaten to feed into broader wholesale and retail prices in coming months.

The ministry said, “Recent moderation in global crude oil prices to below US$100 in early November & strengthening of the rupee following robust capital inflows may provide some relief from imported inflationary pressures, contingent upon the persistence of this trend."

It said that the upcoming inflation prints may face upside risks on higher food and non-food item demand. The Indian economy enters the coming months with firm domestic momentum. In addition to that, consumption demand is resilient, and private investment is broadening gradually.

Domestic economic activity is expected to sustain its momentum into Q3 FY27. The evolving geopolitical situation and uncertainty surrounding global trade policies could weigh on the outlook. According to the ministry, the Indian economy has adequate buffers to navigate emerging challenges.

data.title: E2E Networks bags ₹136 crore international order from AI foundation model developer
data.description:
Cloud infrastructure company E2E Networks Ltd on Saturday (November 28) said it has secured an international order worth $14.63 million (approximately ₹136 crore) from an AI foundation model developer for providing graphics processing unit (GPU) cloud computing and related services.

The order has a committed value of $14.63 million and will be executed over a period of 36 months, according to the company's regulatory filing. E2E Networks said it has executed an agreement with the international entity for the provision of GPU cloud computing and related services.

The company clarified that neither its promoters, promoter group, nor group companies have any interest in the entity awarding the contract. The order does not fall under related-party transactions.

Back in August this year, E2E Networks Ltd said it has entered into a binding term sheet with a sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) company based in India for providing NVIDIA Blackwell cloud graphics processing units (GPUs) and allied services.

The arrangement has an aggregate contract value of approximately ₹1,000 crore, excluding applicable taxes, and remains valid until June 2029. The company said the engagement is a significant milestone in its strategy of signing up longer-term customers.

:....we wish to inform you that the company has entered into the binding term sheet with a Sovereign AI company based in India requiring high-performance computing infrastructure, for the provision of NVIDIA Blackwell cloud GPUs and allied services.

The arrangement has an aggregate contract value of approximately ₹1,000 crore (exclusive of applicable taxes) and remains valid up to June, 2029," according to a stock exchange filing.

Under the term sheet, E2E Networks will provide long-term AI infrastructure comprising cloud GPUs and allied services. The customer is a domestic entity, and the services are to be provided up to June 2029.

Shares of E2E Networks Ltd ended at ₹499.10, up by ₹23.00, or 4.83%, on the BSE.

data.title: BlackRock Bitcoin ETF Loses $2.8 Billion in Eight Consecutive Trading Sessions
data.description:
Key takeaways

  • US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows in eight straight sessions from November 17 to 27, totaling about $3.44 billion.
  • BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for about $2.79 billion of that, roughly 81%.
  • Friday’s shortened session still saw $389 million leave the funds, including $327.2 million from IBIT.
  • IBIT’s Friday outflow was barely below Wednesday’s $329.7 million, despite the shorter trading window.
  • ETF redemptions are not BlackRock selling its own Bitcoin, and the data does not show who is redeeming.

The BlackRock Bitcoin ETF has recorded nearly $2.8 billion in net withdrawals across eight consecutive trading sessions, accounting for approximately 81% of the capital leaving US spot Bitcoin ETFs over the period.

The latest figures from Farside Investors show that US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered $389 million in combined net outflows on Friday, November 27, extending a withdrawal streak that began on November 17.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $327.2 million of Friday’s withdrawals.

Despite a shortened trading session following Thanksgiving, investors continued reducing their exposure through the largest Bitcoin ETF in the US.

BlackRock Accounts for Most of the Bitcoin ETF Withdrawals

Combined net withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin ETFs reached $3.44 billion over the eight trading sessions between November 17 and November 27.

Of that amount, approximately $2.79 billion came from BlackRock’s IBIT.

The fund recorded its heaviest withdrawals during this period on November 19 and 20, when investors redeemed a net $541.1 million and $544.7 million, respectively.

Net flows of US spot Bitcoin ETFs during the eight-session withdrawal streak. *Shortened post-Thanksgiving session; US markets were closed on November 26. Data: Farside Investors. Visualization: NewsBTC.

The concentration of withdrawals in IBIT is particularly important when interpreting aggregate Bitcoin ETF figures. Activity in a single fund has dominated the broader market’s recent net flows.

BlackRock’s size naturally makes it more likely to account for substantial movements of capital. Its share of the outflows, therefore, should not automatically be interpreted as evidence that investors are specifically losing confidence in BlackRock.

Has Bitcoin ETF Selling Actually Slowed?

Friday’s $389 million in combined net outflows was lower than Wednesday’s $453 million, but the improvement was relatively modest.

BlackRock’s figures were particularly revealing. IBIT recorded $327.2 million in net withdrawals on Friday, barely below the $329.7 million recorded during Wednesday’s full trading session.

The shortened post-Thanksgiving trading window makes the comparison even less encouraging.

CoinGlass’s historical ETF flow data also illustrates how recent withdrawals contrast with the substantial inflows recorded during earlier stages of Bitcoin’s rally.

A smaller daily outflow does not necessarily signal that investors are returning. It may simply mean less capital left the funds during that particular session.

What Does This Mean for Bitcoin’s Recovery?

As NewsBTC previously reported, persistent withdrawals from spot Bitcoin ETFs have complicated the cryptocurrency’s attempts to establish a sustainable recovery.

It is important, however, to distinguish ETF redemptions from direct selling by BlackRock itself.

IBIT holds Bitcoin on behalf of its shareholders. Net withdrawals reflect activity within the fund’s creation and redemption mechanism, rather than necessarily representing a decision by BlackRock to sell Bitcoin from its own corporate balance sheet.

The figures also do not reveal whether the investors behind the redemptions are institutions, financial advisers or retail participants.

Monday’s trading session, the final US session of November, will offer another opportunity to assess whether demand for Bitcoin exposure is beginning to stabilize.

For now, Friday’s figures provide little evidence that the withdrawal pressure has materially eased. BlackRock’s fund experienced almost the same net outflows as Wednesday, despite a shorter trading session.

data.title: Musk says Google is interested in renting more computing capacity from SpaceX
data.description:
Elon Musk said on Saturday in a post on X that Google was interested in renting more computing capacity from SpaceX , without providing further details.

Musk, SpaceX and Google did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

SpaceX already has a multi-year cloud services agreement with Google, signed before its blockbuster IPO. Google will pay SpaceX $920 million monthly from October this year to June 2029, as per the terms of the deal announced in June.

The compute capacity includes about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs, CPUs, memory and other related components.

Demand for computing infrastructure has surged since generative AI services were introduced, prompting technology companies to invest heavily in data centers equipped with advanced chips from Nvidia and other manufacturers.

In May, rival Anthropic said that it had reached a deal to tap SpaceX's computing resources.

In a regulatory filing in June, SpaceX disclosed compute-capacity agreements with Anthropic and Google worth more than $70 billion on aggregate.

SpaceX is also increasing its computing capacity beyond its existing Memphis-area hub. It said this month it would spend more than $74 billion in a planned investment at a new supercomputer facility at Starbase in the Rio Grande Valley in Texas, and a second campus in Cochise County, Arizona.

data.title: Gene Munster Admits Focusing On AI Fundamentals Was A Mistake, But Believes Investors Buying NVDA Stock Now Could Be Rewarded
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said the fundamentals underpinning the AI trade remain stronger than expected, pointing to Nvidia’s latest outlook and spending commitments from major hyperscalers.
  • He noted that Nvidia's calendar 2027 growth expectations stood at 75%, above Wall Street's 70% estimate.
  • Munster also highlighted positive spending commentary from major cloud companies and the enormous investments planned across the AI ecosystem.

The artificial intelligence trade continues to face turbulence, with investor sentiment struggling to keep pace with the industry's growth prospects. But Deepwater Asset Management partner Gene Munster believes the recent weakness could present an opportunity for investors willing to look beyond the near-term uncertainty.

During an interview with CNBC, Munster acknowledged that his own approach to the AI sell-off may have overlooked an important part of the market equation, even as he maintained his conviction in the sector's longer-term prospects, including Nvidia Corp. (NVDA).

Nvidia shares gained nearly 1% in Friday’s regular session, but edged lower by 0.5% during the after-hours trade.

Munster Admits Focusing On AI Fundamentals Was A Mistake

Munster said the fundamentals underpinning the AI trade remain stronger than expected, pointing to Nvidia’s latest outlook and spending commitments from major hyperscalers.

He noted that Nvidia's calendar 2027 growth expectations stood at 75%, above Wall Street's 70% estimate. He also highlighted positive spending commentary from major cloud companies and the enormous investments planned across the AI ecosystem.

However, Munster said he had made a mistake by focusing too heavily on fundamentals while overlooking investor psychology.

"I've been buying Nvidia. I bought after Jensen left. Stock was higher at that point. And the mistake I made was focusing just on the fundamentals," he said.

He added that the AI trade remains largely in the "penalty box," with investors yet to regain confidence despite the industry's strong underlying performance.

Munster stopped short of calling a market bottom but said investors with the conviction to own AI stocks today could be rewarded a year from now.

AI Adoption Still Below 1%, Says Munster

Munster believes the AI investment cycle remains in its early stages, with adoption still below 1%.

He pointed to SAP reportedly cutting around 10% of its workforce as an example of how AI-driven changes could reshape businesses and industries over time.

The analyst also highlighted persistent demand for AI chips, arguing that supply constraints remain significant.

"If you want to order a chip today, you're probably not getting it until the end of 2028," Munster said.

He also discussed the longer-term prospects of OpenAI and Anthropic, arguing that both frontier AI companies are positioned to benefit as businesses increasingly monetize their models across enterprise and consumer markets.

Dan Ives Also Sticks To His AI Bull Case

Munster isn't alone in maintaining a bullish outlook despite the market volatility.

Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said his AI investment thesis remains intact, even after putting the industry through a three-part stress test.

Ives asked investors to consider a scenario in which 20% of planned data centers never get built, revenue through the Asia export loophole disappears, and financing for AI infrastructure falls by 25%.

Even under those conditions, he said he remains bullish on the AI investment opportunity over the next two to three years.

Ives also estimated that China and the Asia loophole account for no more than 15% to 20% of revenue, describing the exposure as manageable.

Together, the views from Munster and Ives suggest that while investor sentiment remains fragile, some prominent technology bulls continue to see the recent AI stock weakness as an opportunity rather than the beginning of the end of the boom.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.41%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) declined 0.06%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) gained 0.23%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) gained nearly 4% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) rose over 2%.

data.title: KuCoin Advances Australian Engagement at CryptoCon Sydney, Spotlighting Global Infrastructure and Local Accountability
data.description:
SYDNEY, Nov. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KuCoin highlighted the importance of connecting global exchange capabilities with local responsibilities at CryptoCon Sydney at ICC Sydney. During the panel "Global Infrastructure, Local Accountability: Where Exchanges Fit in Crypto's Next Phase," KuCoin CMO Skylar W and Managing Director of KuCoin in Australia James Pinch discussed how exchanges can respond to broader financial needs through infrastructure investment, market-specific governance and local delivery. They were joined by Zach Ahmajani, Head of Operations at KuCoin in Australia, in a discussion moderated by Lydia Ward, Growth Manager of KuCoin in Australia.

Skylar described an industry in which trading volume, liquidity and asset selection remain important, but expectations increasingly extend to the infrastructure and operating standards behind those services. She connected KuCoin's investment in security and transparency through its $2 Billion Trust Project with the development of its global compliance framework and institutional services. "Global capabilities are the starting point. What matters is how the product works locally, with clear responsibilities from day one," said Skylar W. Her remarks also highlighted continued work on trading architecture and security infrastructure to support performance and resilience as financial activity becomes more demanding.

During the discussion, Skylar also introduced KuCoin 5.0 as an example of how those investments translate into tangible improvements for users. Launched under the "Trust, Built-in." initiative, the platform-wide upgrade offers distinct Lite and Pro experiences and a single point of access to AI assistance across the platform. It also introduces a Unified Trading Account that allows eligible users at VIP1 and above to manage funds and trade across spot, margin and futures from one account.

James brought that discussion back to the tasks users need to complete. Drawing on a focus group involving people who had purchased crypto in the previous 12 to 24 months, he described participants using digital assets to pay vendors and send money overseas. While those observations reflected the group rather than all users, they illustrated why exchanges need to consider the full journey of moving and using funds. "Some of the people we spoke to were buying crypto because they had a payment or transfer to make," said James Pinch. "Banks and exchanges each have a role, and the opportunity is to improve how those services meet the needs of people and businesses."

The discussion connected these changing needs with a practical requirement: global infrastructure must translate into services that reflect the market they serve. For KuCoin, that means combining technology and product expertise with local understanding, clearly identifying service-provider responsibilities and distinguishing global capabilities from services available through the relevant entity. Security measures, reserve disclosures and independent assessments contribute to that approach by giving users information about platform practices within defined scopes.

This emphasis on accountability extended to "The Future of Finance in Australia: A Government & Regulatory Roundtable," where James Kwan, KuCoin Australia's legal lead, joined representatives from the Australian Taxation Office (ATO), the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC), and DECA. The session explored priorities for the responsible development of Australia's digital asset market, placing regulatory dialogue and governance alongside the industry's technology and product development.

KuCoin's participation followed the opening of its Australian programme with Global Brand Ambassador Adam Scott on 23 November. Building on its collaboration with the convention in 2025, its three-year partnership with CryptoCon Sydney provides an ongoing forum for engagement with Australian users and industry partners. Together with its Sydney office and local leadership team established in 2025, the partnership supports KuCoin's long-term approach to bringing global resources into services shaped by local expertise and needs.

About KuCoin

Founded in 2017, KuCoin is a leading global crypto platform built on trust and security, serving over 45 million users across 200+ countries and regions. Known for its reliability and user-first approach, the platform builds trust into every layer of the user experience, combining advanced technology, deep liquidity, and strong security safeguards to deliver a seamless trading experience. KuCoin globally provides access to 1,000+ digital assets through a broad product suite and remains committed to building a secure, transparent, compliant, and user-centric ecosystem for the future of finance, backed by SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, ISO 22301:2019 and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certifications. In recent years, KuCoin has continued to strengthen its global compliance foundation, marked by key milestones including AUSTRAC registration in Australia, a MiCA license in Europe, and regulatory progress in other markets.

Learn more at www.kucoin.com.

data.title: Kinzey Capital Management Announces Analysis of UK October CPI Release
data.description:
Singapore, Singapore, November 28th, 2026, FinanceWire

Kinzey Capital Management announced its analysis of the UK’s October inflation data, highlighting that consumer price inflation reached 3.6%, the highest level in a year, driven mainly by rising fuel, energy and tobacco costs. The firm noted that stable core and services inflation indicate underlying domestic price pressures remain contained, shaping market expectations for future Bank of England interest rate decisions.

Fuel costs push UK consumer price inflation to 3.6% in the latest official figures, up from 3.5% a month earlier and the highest reading in a year. The Office for National Statistics figure matches the median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists but sits below the 3.7% the Bank of England had projected for the month. Kinzey Capital Management Pte. Ltd. looks past that headline to the gauges of domestic price pressure beneath it, which hold steady.

Crude oil supplies the main upward force, with prices up around 20% over the month on tensions in the Middle East. The jump lifts transport and factory costs alike, taking motor fuel inflation to 33.2% from 29.8% the month before, its highest in more than four years, as diesel prices hit a record. Compared with the prior month, transport inflation accelerates to 7.5% from 6.6% and goods inflation to 3.5% from 3.2%, its highest in more than three years. Food price inflation eases to 0.9% from the previous month’s 1.3%, its lowest in more than five years.

Household energy bills and tobacco add further pressure, with Ofgem’s price cap 4% higher for the current quarter. Higher wholesale gas prices tied to the Middle East conflict account for most of that change, which lifts the typical dual-fuel household bill from $2,178.5 to $2,257.1 a year. Gas bills rise about 8% for the quarter, while the removal of VAT from domestic electricity bills holds electricity costs broadly flat. Tobacco duty rose at the start of the quarter alongside a new duty on vaping products, adding close to $2.9 per 100 cigarettes above the usual RPI-linked increase. Tobacco prices climb 5.2% on the month and 12.4% on a year earlier, the highest annual rate in almost two years.

The underlying measures show no such move, with core inflation, which excludes food and energy, holding at 2.8% for a second consecutive month. Services inflation, which the Bank of England watches for signs of domestic price pressure, matches its previous reading at 3.7%, below the 4.4% recorded nine months earlier, while core has eased from 3.1% over the same span. Both remain far beneath the peaks of three years ago, when core touched 7.1% and services 7.4%.

Kinzey Capital Management treats that gap between the headline and the underlying measures as the most telling feature of the release. David Nilson, the firm’s Director of Private Clients, reads the stability of core and services inflation as confirmation that the latest rise “sits mostly in fuel and energy, not in wages or domestic pricing”. That distinction separates a cost shock arriving from outside the economy from one generated within it, and the core measures so far show no sign of the latter.

The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by a quarter point to 4% earlier this month, its first increase in three years. Traders have since scaled back bets on a further rise at the next policy meeting, and sterling has eased. The shift suggests a market that reads steady core and services inflation as a limit on how far the central bank can tighten while energy costs climb. Nilson presents his own assessment as “one reading of the data, not a forecast of what the Bank does next”.

The Bank’s own projections put inflation at around 5% by the middle of next year as higher wholesale energy costs feed through to household bills. Officials note limited evidence so far of broader effects on wages and non-energy prices. In an adverse case where the Middle East conflict pushes oil prices higher still, the Bank places inflation at 6.2% in the same year, though both figures are projections across a range rather than guarantees.

Ofgem is due in the coming days to confirm the price cap that applies from the turn of the year. Cornwall Insight expects that cap to rise 26%, adding $580.3 to the typical annual dual-fuel bill, with some households due to receive a $131 Budget payment towards the increase. Food price inflation, projected near 4.75% by mid-way through next year, and wage growth will show whether fuel-led pressure spreads into domestic pricing. Kinzey Capital Management reads the latest print as one point in that longer sequence, measuring what each release confirms against the obligations its portfolios carry.

Kinzey Capital Management, on the Record

Kinzey Capital Management is a Singapore-based discretionary manager whose multi-asset portfolios combine shares, bonds, funds and cash in a single book for private clients, companies, families and foundations. Each portfolio is shaped by what its capital must achieve, when it may be needed and how much fluctuation it can bear, with instruments then selected to match. Growth Portfolios, Income and Withdrawals, Corporate Reserves and Joint and Family Accounts remain in place while the capital’s duty endures, whereas Concentrated Shareholdings and Second-Opinion Reviews are single engagements built around existing holdings. Its reports assess every portfolio against the duty assigned to it. The firm is registered as Kinzey Capital Management Pte. data.title: Weather, supply uncertainties may accelerate India inflation, report says
data.description:
India's inflation could pick up in the coming months due to weather and supply-related uncertainties, although moderating oil prices and a stronger rupee could help contain price pressures, the government said in its monthly economic report.

Here are more details from the report released on Saturday.

  • Festivities extending to November and the onset of the wedding season in India could accelerate inflation in the month ahead due to higher costs of food and non-food items

  • Continuing conflict in the Middle East may keep oil import bills and maritime freight rates volatile

  • The evolving geopolitical situation coupled with uncertainty around global trade policies, could weigh on India's external sector outlook

  • Domestic demand and industrial activity continue to underpin growth

  • Resilient domestic fundamentals and adequate macroeconomic buffers leave the Indian economy well placed to navigate emerging challenges

  • India's annual retail inflation in October surged to 6.09% in October, breaching the central bank's 6% limit for the first time under the new series, over rising food prices.

data.title: OpenAI’s 457 MW TensorWave Deal Could Be Worth Up To $9.1B, Say Analysts: What It Means For AMD Stock
data.description:
Key points:
  • Announced on Nov. 16, the agreement will see TensorWave provide OpenAI with dedicated AI computing capacity across multiple U.S. data center locations.
  • The infrastructure will use AMD's Instinct MI455X GPUs in its Helios rack-scale systems, supporting large-scale AI training and inference workloads.
  • The deployment is expected to begin bringing capacity online in the first half of 2027, with full deployment targeted for early 2028.

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) could be looking at another multibillion-dollar opportunity in the artificial intelligence infrastructure market after OpenAI signed a major computing capacity agreement with AMD-backed cloud provider TensorWave, analysts at IO Fund said in a recent note.

The six-year agreement covers 457 megawatts of dedicated AI infrastructure powered by AMD's Instinct MI455X GPUs. While the companies have not disclosed the contract's value, an estimate from IO Fund suggests the hardware deployment could represent an opportunity worth as much as $9.1 billion for AMD.

AMD shares gained nearly 5% in Friday’s regular trading, but edged 0.4% lower during the after-hours session.

OpenAI's 457 MW TensorWave Deal: What's Included?

Announced on Nov. 16, the agreement will see TensorWave provide OpenAI with dedicated AI computing capacity across multiple U.S. data center locations. The infrastructure will use AMD's Instinct MI455X GPUs in its Helios rack-scale systems, supporting large-scale AI training and inference workloads.

The deployment is expected to begin bringing capacity online in the first half of 2027, with full deployment targeted for early 2028.

It is also TensorWave's largest deployment contract to date and makes it the first publicly named neocloud infrastructure provider under OpenAI's previously announced six-gigawatt partnership with AMD.

OpenAI's CTO for compute, Uday Ruddarraju, said the agreement would advance the company's existing partnership with AMD.

How Much Could AMD Make From The OpenAI Deal?

Although neither OpenAI nor TensorWave has disclosed the financial terms, IO Fund estimates that the 457 MW deployment could translate into approximately $4.6 billion to $9.1 billion in AMD hardware.

The estimate draws on AMD CEO Lisa Su's characterization of gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure as a double-digit-billion-dollar revenue opportunity, with the estimate ranging between $10 billion and $20 billion per gigawatt.

However, this is not the disclosed value of the contract. TensorWave is also likely to be AMD's direct hardware buyer, while the total infrastructure investment would include equipment beyond AMD chips.

First capacity is expected in the first half of 2027, potentially making the deal a contributor to AMD's revenue growth next year rather than its current-quarter results, the firm noted.

AMD expects revenue to grow by more than 80% in 2027, with its data center business playing an increasingly important role. Su has also indicated that the company has secured additional supply to support anticipated growth.

IO Fund Says OpenAI's AMD Bet Comes With Execution And Dilution Risks

The deal adds a deployment milestone to OpenAI's broader commitment to deploy six GW of AMD GPUs. However, neither company has explicitly confirmed whether the entire 457 MW deployment counts toward that commitment.

IO Fund also noted that there are concerns around the project’s execution. TensorWave currently operates a cluster of approximately 8,000 GPUs and will need to scale substantially to deliver hundreds of megawatts of capacity within the targeted timeline.

What Retail Investors Think Of AMD Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around AMD trended in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

AMD stock is up 98% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 7% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 6%.

data.title: BPCL board approves ₹1.27 lakh crore refinery & petrochemical complex in Andhra Pradesh
data.description:
State-owned Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) on Saturday (November 28) received board approval to set up a greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, with an estimated capital expenditure of ₹1.27 lakh crore, subject to government, statutory and regulatory approvals.

The project will be developed through a wholly owned subsidiary (WOS) of BPCL and will have a proposed crude oil processing capacity of 9 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA), along with a 1.5 MMTPA mixed-feed ethylene cracker and downstream petrochemical units. The combined throughput of the complex will be 10.5 MMTPA.

The estimated project cost is ₹1,26,656 crore, with an estimation range of plus or minus 20%. The scheduled commercial operation of the project is estimated for July 2032.

The BPCL board has also approved an equity infusion of up to ₹44,330 crore into the wholly owned subsidiary in one or more tranches. This includes an earlier approved equity contribution of up to ₹4,900 crore.

The proposed equity infusion is subject to approval from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) and other applicable approvals. The project will be financed through a combination of equity and debt, with financing arrangements through lenders currently under finalisation.

BPCL Refinery Project

BPCL currently has an installed refining capacity of 35.3 MMTPA, with capacity utilisation of 116.6% in FY26. The proposed project will add 9 MMTPA of crude processing capacity and include a 1.5 MMTPA mixed-feed ethylene cracker. The integrated complex will have a petrochemical intensity of around 34%.

According to the company, the project is intended to address its widening deficit in key transportation fuels and India's growing petrochemical supply gap.

The integrated refinery-petrochemical configuration is expected to strengthen product availability, reduce import dependence on key polymers, improve value realisation through refinery-petrochemical integration and diversify earnings. It is also aimed at supporting downstream chemical and polymer industries.

On Friday (November 27), shares of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited ended at ₹308.25, up by ₹0.60, or 0.20%, on the BSE.
